title: is handed the build's release label for the app, not Electron's version
why: Settings and Copy diagnostics read Electron's version, package.json's 1.0.0, so a candidate never says which candidate it is.

title: is handed the build's release label for the app, not Electron's version
why: The macOS About panel loses its version, and AppKit shows the bundle's 1.0.0 for a candidate.

title: is handed the build's release label for the app, not Electron's version
why: The About panel's build version falls back to CFBundleVersion, so a candidate's About box says "1.0.0-rc.2 (1.0.0)".

title: drops the oldest lines and keeps the newest
why: A trim that keeps the head of the log and drops its end: the newest lines, the ones a report is about, would be the ones lost.

title: drops the oldest lines and keeps the newest
why: The budget never compared with: a copy of any size is returned whole, and a long one is too long for an issue.

title: leaves a copy under the budget as it was, with no line saying otherwise
why: The comparison reversed to always trim: a copy that fits is cut and carries a trim line it should not.

title: keeps the five head sections byte for byte
why: The line under the heading left out: a trimmed copy would say nothing of what it lost, and the reader would take the logs for whole.

title: drops the oldest map reports once the logs are down to their floor, and not before
why: The floor removed: the logs are emptied before any map report goes, and a report-heavy session loses its logs, the most diagnostic part of the copy.

title: takes lines from below the floor only when nothing else is left to take
why: The last step left out: when even the floor does not fit, nothing more is taken and the copy stays over the budget.

title: reads correctly for a log of one line, and for one of none
why: The plural kept for one line: the trim line reads "its last 1 lines".
